# raglab

The **agentic-search / RAG orchestration layer on top of [`ir`](https://github.com/i2mint/ir)** (the retrieval substrate).

`raglab` turns a retrieval substrate into a **Composable Search Agent**: a small
set of injected **roles** — Planner, Formulator, Retriever, Evaluator, Reranker,
Citer — wired by a control loop. The loop’s defining feature is the **back-edge**
(*evaluator → reformulate*): when results aren’t good enough, the agent rewrites
the query and searches again. That back-edge is what makes it an *agent* rather
than a fixed pipeline (DAG).

```bash
pip install raglab
```

> **Fresh start (v0.2.0+).** This repo took over the `raglab` PyPI name. The
> earlier backend (PyPI 0.0.x–0.1.x) was renamed and now lives at
> [addaix/raglab_bak](https://github.com/addaix/raglab_bak) (PyPI:
> [`raglab_bak`](https://pypi.org/project/raglab_bak/)). The API below is the new
> agent layer.

---

## Quick start

The default agent runs **fully offline** — no LLM, no network. Point it at one or
more `ir` corpora and call it like a function; you get back ranked
[`ir.SearchHit`](https://github.com/i2mint/ir)s.

```python
import ir
import raglab

# Register named ir corpora as the agent's sources, then search across them.
sources = raglab.ir_sources("skills", "reports", mode="hybrid")
agent = raglab.make_search_agent(sources)
results = agent("how do I deploy the app")  # -> list[ir.SearchHit], ranked
```

A self-contained, runnable example (build a tiny corpus, search it):

```python
import ir
from ir.store import CorpusStore
import raglab

docs = {
    "deploy": "deploy the app to the server with systemd units",
    "embed": "embed text with a model and cache the vectors",
    "search": "vector similarity search with metadata filters",
}
corpus = ir.build(
    ir.CorpusSource.from_mapping(docs, name="t", strategy=ir.WholeText()),
    store=CorpusStore.memory(),
    embedder="light",  # numpy-only, no model download
)

agent = raglab.make_search_agent({"t": ir.as_retriever(corpus, k=3)})
results = agent("deploy the app to the server")
results[0].artifact_id  # -> "deploy"
```

`sources` is any `Mapping[name, Retriever]`. Build it with
[`raglab.ir_sources(*names, **defaults)`](), with `ir.retrievers()` (a
lazy live view over everything ir has registered), or by hand:
`{"skills": ir.as_retriever("skills")}`.

---

## The mental model

```default
           ┌─────────── back-edge (re-query when insufficient) ──────────┐
           ▼                                                             │
  Query → Planner → [SubTask] → Formulator → [LowLevelQuery] → Retriever(s)
                                                                   │
                                          accumulated hits ◄───────┘
                                                   │
                                            Evaluator ──► Judgement(relevant, sufficient, refinement)
                                                   │              └─ refinement ⟲ back-edge
                                          (sufficient / budget hit)
                                                   ▼
                                       Reranker (fan-in) → Citer → ranked results
```

The **loop is fixed**; every *decision* in it is an injected **role** (a plain
callable satisfying a `Protocol`). v1 ships every role with a sensible default,
so the simple path — `make_search_agent(sources)("query")` — just works. You turn
capabilities on by swapping in richer roles.

| Role           | Decides                                   | Default (no-LLM)                                 | Inject an LLM version to…                           |
|----------------|-------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| **Planner**    | decompose query → sub-tasks, pick sources | `single_subtask_planner` (one task, all sources) | split a query into parallel sub-goals               |
| **Formulator** | sub-task → concrete search queries        | `identity_formulator` (verbatim)                 | rewrite / expand / HyDE (`make_llm_formulator`)     |
| **Retriever**  | run one query against one source          | *injected at the leaf* (`ir.as_retriever`)       | add web / SQL / graph backends                      |
| **Evaluator**  | relevance + sufficiency + **back-edge**   | `passthrough_evaluator` (keep all, stop)         | judge sufficiency & re-query (`make_llm_evaluator`) |
| **Reranker**   | final cross-source ordering (fan-in)      | `rrf_reranker` (rank fusion)                     | weight sources, change fusion                       |
| **Citer**      | confirm each result supports its use      | `identity_citer` (no-op)                         | *(generation/verification lives in `srag`)*         |

**`Budget`** bounds the loop (`max_rounds`, `max_sources_per_task`,
`max_results_per_task`) — the safety net under the (harder) sufficiency decision.

---

## Turning on query understanding and the back-edge

Inject the two LLM roles to upgrade the offline slice into a real agent. Both
build their model lazily on [`oa`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/oa) **only when
invoked**, so `import raglab` stays offline.

```python
import raglab

agent = raglab.make_search_agent(
    sources,
    formulator=raglab.make_llm_formulator(),  # rewrite/expand the query (HyDE)
    evaluator=raglab.make_llm_evaluator(),  # sufficiency + the back-edge
)
results = agent("how do I deploy the app")
```

How the Evaluator splits the decision (a load-bearing boundary):

- **Relevance is `ir`’s.** Each round the accumulated hits pass through
  `ir.select` (default strategy `"conservative"` — distractor-robust); the
  committed subset becomes `Judgement.relevant`. LLM relevance scoring is
  known-fragile, so the LLM stays out of it.
- **Sufficiency is the LLM’s.** Informed by ir’s model-free
  `Selection.sufficient` hint, the judge decides whether the committed subset
  actually satisfies the goal. If not, it emits an improved query — a
  `refinement` `SubTask` over the same sources. **That refinement is the
  back-edge.**

Both builders accept an injectable double (`formulate=` / `judge=`) for
deterministic tests, and both **fail safe**: a formulator error falls back to the
raw query (never makes retrieval worse); a judge error returns no refinement
(the loop’s break condition — a failing judge can never spin forever).

---

## Multi-source search and the fan-in reranker

The agent is **multi-source by default**. The loop stamps each hit’s provenance
(`hit.source`), and the default fan-in reranker, `rrf_reranker`, merges
heterogeneous sources **by rank, never by raw score**.

This matters because scores from different corpora / embedders / retrieval modes
are *incommensurable* — a cosine score (~0–1) and a BM25 score (~0–50) cannot be
compared directly. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) sidesteps this: within one source
raw scores order and dedup that source’s hits (one scale, sound); across sources
only **ranks** interact.

```python
# Two sources on different score scales:
#   rrf_reranker (default): interleaves both sources' rank-1 hits first.
#   score_reranker (opt-in): a raw-score sort — only sound when every source
#                            shares one scale (same embedder + mode).
agent = raglab.make_search_agent(sources, reranker=raglab.score_reranker)
```

Colliding `artifact_id`s from different sources stay distinct (identity is
`(source, artifact_id)`). Each fused hit keeps its pre-fusion magnitude in
`metadata["source_score"]`. For per-source trust weights or a custom `rrf_k`:

```python
reranker = raglab.make_rrf_reranker(weights={"skills": 2.0, "web": 0.5}, rrf_k=60)
agent = raglab.make_search_agent(sources, reranker=reranker)
```

---

## Customizing roles

Every role is just a callable matching a `Protocol`, so you can inject your own:

```python
from raglab import SubTask, LowLevelQuery, Judgement, make_search_agent


def my_planner(query, sources):
    # split into two sub-goals over all sources
    return [
        SubTask(goal=g, sources=tuple(sources))
        for g in (query.text, query.text + " examples")
    ]


def my_formulator(task, source):
    return [LowLevelQuery(source=source, query=task.goal, params={"k": 10})]


agent = make_search_agent(sources, planner=my_planner, formulator=my_formulator)
```

A **custom Retriever** is any `callable(query, **params) -> Sequence[ir.SearchHit]`.
It must return `ir.SearchHit` instances (the `Result` alias) — the loop stamps
provenance on its output, so duck-typed hit objects raise at the tagging step.
ir-backed retrievers self-attribute their corpus name.

---

## API at a glance

Everything is exported from the top-level `raglab` namespace.

**Value types** (frozen dataclasses, plain data):

| Type            | Fields                                                              |
|-----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `Query`         | `text`, `constraints`                                               |
| `SubTask`       | `goal`, `sources: tuple[str, ...]`                                  |
| `LowLevelQuery` | `source`, `query`, `params` (per-call retriever overrides)          |
| `Judgement`     | `relevant`, `sufficient`, `refinement: SubTask | None`              |
| `Budget`        | `max_rounds=3`, `max_sources_per_task=4`, `max_results_per_task=50` |
| `Result`        | alias for `ir.SearchHit`                                            |

**Role Protocols** (the open-closed strategy seams): `Planner`, `Formulator`,
`Retriever` (re-exported from `ir`), `Evaluator`, `Reranker`, `Citer`.

**Orchestrator & builders:**

| Name                                                                                     | What it does                                                            |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `make_search_agent(sources, *, planner, formulator, evaluator, reranker, citer, budget)` | Build a `SingleContextAgent` with smart defaults for every role.        |
| `SingleContextAgent`                                                                     | The orchestrator dataclass: one ReAct-style loop, sequential sub-tasks. |
| <a name="sources"></a>`ir_sources(*names, **search_defaults)`                            | A `{name: Retriever}` registry backed by named ir corpora.              |

**Default roles (the no-LLM thin slice):** `single_subtask_planner`,
`identity_formulator`, `passthrough_evaluator`, `score_reranker`, `rrf_reranker`,
`make_rrf_reranker(*, rrf_k, weights, identity)`, `identity_citer`.

**LLM roles:** `make_llm_formulator(*, formulate=None, params=None, **make_kwargs)`,
`make_llm_evaluator(*, judge=None, select_strategy="conservative", select_kwargs=None, prerank=None, prompt=EVALUATION_PROMPT, ...)`,
and the default `EVALUATION_PROMPT` string.

---

## Architecture & boundaries

`raglab` **owns the agent**: the value types, the role Protocols, the control
loop with the back-edge, the budget governor, the source registry, and the
cross-source fan-in.

It **consumes from `ir`** (and does not reimplement): `ir.as_retriever` (corpus →
Retriever), `ir.retrievers()` (the live registry view), `ir.make_llm_formulator`
(the query rewriter), `ir.select` + its `Selection.sufficient` signal (relevance

+ the sufficiency hint), and `ir.fuse_hits` (RRF). The `Result` type and the
  `Retriever` contract are **ir’s** (single source of truth).

**Dependency direction is one-way:** `raglab` imports `ir` (and `oa` for the LLM
roles, lazily); **`ir` never imports `raglab`.** Keeping `oa` opt-in is what lets
`import raglab` stay offline.

What lives **elsewhere:** answer synthesis / generation and the
Citer/Verifier (which needs a *generated claim* to verify) belong in the
RAG/generation layer (`srag`), not the search agent. raglab’s deliverable is
**pointers + extractions**, not an essay.

Where it sits in the ecosystem: **`raglab` → `ir` → {`ef`, `vd`}** — `ir` is the
retrieval substrate, `ef` owns embedders/segmenters, `vd` is the vector-store
facade.

---

## Status & roadmap

Shipped at **0.2.4**: the `SingleContextAgent` control loop with the back-edge,
all six role Protocols, the no-LLM defaults, the LLM Formulator + Evaluator, and
the RRF cross-source fan-in reranker. The roles, value types, and loop are
stable; richer strategies are added behind the same contracts.

The living roadmap is **[issue #2](https://github.com/thorwhalen/raglab/issues/2)**
(Composable Search Agent on ir, the *ir_09* reference design). Not yet built:

- **Budget governor refinements** — the per-task results cap currently truncates
  in arrival order rather than by rank
  ([#5](https://github.com/thorwhalen/raglab/issues/5)); termination as a
  separately injected policy is planned.
- **PurposeStore** — persistent, purpose-indexed memory overlay
  ([#6](https://github.com/thorwhalen/raglab/issues/6)). There is no cross-run
  memory today.
- **`MultiAgentAgent`** — one subagent per sub-task/source (breadth-first, ~15×
  cost); promotion swaps only the orchestrator, keeping role contracts identical.

---

## House style

Functional over OOP; SOLID when OOP; facades, SSOT, dependency injection;
progressive disclosure; keyword-only args beyond the third positional;
`collections.abc` + frozen `dataclass`es; `Protocol`s for the role seams. Tests
are hermetic (fake retrievers, injected LLM doubles) with a few end-to-end checks
over a real `ir` corpus using the light, numpy-only embedder.

# _autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md

# raglab.agent

The Composable Search Agent — roles wired by a control loop (ir_09).

`raglab` is the \*\*orchestration layer on top of `ir`** (the retrieval substrate).
This module is the v1 foundation: the immutable value types, the role *Protocols*
(open-closed strategy seams), and a `SingleContextAgent` whose fixed control loop
is fully parametrized by injected roles. Concrete tools live at the leaves — an
`ir` corpus becomes one `Retriever` via `ir.as_retriever()`.

The agent is **multi-source by default**: the loop stamps each hit’s
provenance (`hit.source`), and the fan-in [`Reranker`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Reranker) —
[`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.rrf_reranker) — merges heterogeneous sources by *rank*, never by raw
score (scores from different corpora / embedders / modes are incommensurable;
ir_07/ir_08). Raw magnitudes order and dedup hits *within* one source, and the
loop’s pool always carries them; fused (ordinal) scores appear only at the
fan-in boundary.

The shape follows ir_09 §3/§6: a small set of named roles —
`Planner / Formulator / Retriever / Evaluator / Reranker / Citer` — and a loop
whose defining feature is the **back-edge** (evaluator → reformulate) that makes
it an *agent* rather than a DAG. v1 ships the loop with smart defaults (a trivial
planner + a pass-through evaluator), so the thin slice runs end-to-end with no
LLM; turning on the back-edge is just injecting an LLM `Evaluator` that returns
a `refinement` (ir_09 §8 step 3).

Progressive disclosure: [`make_search_agent()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.make_search_agent) gives sensible defaults for
every role, so the simple path is `make_search_agent(sources)("query")`.

Dependency direction is one-way: `raglab` imports `ir`; `ir` never imports
`raglab`. The `Result` type and the `Retriever` contract are ir’s (SSOT).

### *class* raglab.agent.GradedLabel(level, is_about, is_supported, is_useful, evidence_quote='', facet=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A graded verdict on one candidate (raglab#8): a level, three axes, the evidence.

`level` is one of the evaluator’s ordered levels (best first). The axes are
Self-RAG’s: `is_about` (topical, ISREL), `is_supported` (the content
actually establishes it, not a lexical mention: ISSUP) and `is_useful`
(ISUSE). `evidence_quote` is a verbatim span of the candidate’s content
backing the level; `facet` names the sub-goal it was judged against.

### *class* raglab.agent.Judgement(relevant, sufficient, refinement=None, graded=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

An evaluator’s verdict over a round’s results.

`relevant` is the kept subset; `sufficient` says whether to stop; a
non-`None` `refinement` is the **back-edge** — the next sub-task to
re-query with. The pass-through default returns `sufficient=True` and no
refinement (no loop). `graded` is optional and additive: a graded
evaluator maps each judged `artifact_id` to its [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel);
binary evaluators leave it empty.

### *class* raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery(source, query, params=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One concrete query against one source.

`query` is the text handed to the source’s `Retriever`; `params`
are per-call retriever overrides (e.g. `mode` / `filter` / `k` for an
ir corpus). A formulator turns a [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask) into these.

### *class* raglab.agent.PoolCap(\*args, \*\*kwargs)

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Bound the pool the evaluator sees to at most `limit` results.

A governor decision (which hits survive the budget), injected like every other
role so a strategy can be swapped without touching the loop. It must return
hits **unchanged** — never re-scored — because the pool keeps raw per-source
magnitudes until the fan-in reranker.

Identity formulator: the sub-goal verbatim as one query (no rewrite/HyDE).

  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery)]

#### planner(sources)

Trivial planner: one sub-task over *all* registered sources, no decomposition.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask)]

#### pool_cap(limit)

Keep at most `limit` hits, taking the best of each source in turn (the default).

Groups the pool by `hit.source` (in first-arrival order; untagged hits are one
group), collapses each group to one hit per artifact (its best surface, as
`ir.base.best_per_artifact()` does), orders the group best-first by its own raw
score – sound, since one source is one score scale – and deals hits round-robin
across the groups. So a late source’s strong hits are never cut before the evaluator
sees them, a duplicate never takes a slot, and no score ever crosses a source
boundary or is rewritten (unlike pre-ranking with the RRF reranker, whose fused
ordinal scores must never re-enter the pool). The output is in that dealt order
whatever the pool’s size. A missing or NaN score sorts last in its source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

#### reranker()

Cross-source merge (the default fan-in): fuse by rank, never by raw score.

Groups the accumulated pool by `hit.source` and delegates the merge to
`ir.fuse_hits()` (ir is the SSOT for hit operations): within each
source raw scores order and dedup that source’s hits — one scale, sound —
and across sources only **ranks** interact (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), so
heterogeneous embedders / modes can never mis-order the merge, and
colliding `artifact_id`s from different sources stay distinct results
(identity is `(source, artifact_id)`).

A single-source pool (or an untagged one — hits with no `source`) keeps
its raw scores and exactly [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.score_reranker)’s ordering; fused,
rank-derived scores only appear when there is genuinely something to fuse.
Each fused hit keeps its pre-fusion magnitude as
`metadata["source_score"]`. For per-source weights, another `rrf_k`,
or opt-in cross-source duplicate merging, use [`make_rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.make_rrf_reranker).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### *class* raglab.agent.SubTask(goal, sources)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A planner’s unit of work: a sub-goal bound to a set of registered sources.

### raglab.agent.arrival_order_cap(results, limit)

Keep the first `limit` hits in arrival order (source order x query order).

The pre-governor behaviour: a late source’s strong hits can be cut before the
evaluator sees them. Kept as an explicit opt-in (`pool_cap=arrival_order_cap`).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.agent.identity_citer(results)

No-op citer (verification needs a generated claim — that lives in srag).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.agent.identity_formulator(task, source)

Identity formulator: the sub-goal verbatim as one query (no rewrite/HyDE).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery)]

### raglab.agent.ir_sources(\*names, \*\*search_defaults)

A source registry `{name: Retriever}` backed by named `ir` corpora.

Each name is bound to `ir.as_retriever(name, **search_defaults)`, opened
eagerly. For the *lazy* live view over everything registered (a corpus
opens only when its key is first used), use `ir.retrievers()` instead —
the agent accepts either, or any `Mapping[name, Retriever]`.
`search_defaults` (e.g. `mode="hybrid"`) apply to every source.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]]]

### raglab.agent.make_rrf_reranker(, rrf_k=60, weights=None, identity=None)

A parametrized [`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.rrf_reranker) (per-source trust weights, `rrf_k`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **rrf_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – the RRF rank constant (standard default 60).
  * **weights** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – optional per-source trust dial, by source name (default 1.0
    each) — biases the merge without ever comparing raw scores.
  * **identity** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`SearchHit`], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – opt-in cross-source duplicate detection (e.g. `"pointer"`)
    — see `ir.retrieve.Identity`. Default: never merge across
    sources.
* **Return type:**
  [`Reranker`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Reranker)

### raglab.agent.make_search_agent(sources, , planner=None, formulator=None, evaluator=None, reranker=None, citer=None, budget=None, pool_cap=None, run_log=None)

Build a [`SingleContextAgent`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SingleContextAgent) over *sources* with smart defaults.

`sources` is a `Mapping[name, Retriever]` — e.g.
`{"skills": ir.as_retriever("skills")}`, [`ir_sources()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.ir_sources), or the lazy
`ir.retrievers()` view. Every role defaults to its no-LLM thin-slice
implementation, so `make_search_agent(sources)("query")` just works;
inject an LLM `formulator` / `evaluator` to turn on rewriting and the
back-edge. Pass a `run_log` (any callable taking a [`RoundRecord`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.RoundRecord), e.g.
`list.append`) to record what each round decided.

A custom `Retriever` must return `ir.SearchHit` instances (the
`Result` alias): the loop stamps provenance (`hit.source`) on its
output, so duck-typed hit objects raise at the tagging step.

* **Return type:**
  [`SingleContextAgent`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SingleContextAgent)

### raglab.agent.passthrough_evaluator(task, results)

Pass-through critic: keep everything, declare sufficient, never re-query.

* **Return type:**
  [`Judgement`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Judgement)

### raglab.agent.rank_fair_cap(results, limit)

Keep at most `limit` hits, taking the best of each source in turn (the default).

Groups the pool by `hit.source` (in first-arrival order; untagged hits are one
group), collapses each group to one hit per artifact (its best surface, as
`ir.base.best_per_artifact()` does), orders the group best-first by its own raw
score – sound, since one source is one score scale – and deals hits round-robin
across the groups. So a late source’s strong hits are never cut before the evaluator
sees them, a duplicate never takes a slot, and no score ever crosses a source
boundary or is rewritten (unlike pre-ranking with the RRF reranker, whose fused
ordinal scores must never re-enter the pool). The output is in that dealt order
whatever the pool’s size. A missing or NaN score sorts last in its source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.agent.rrf_reranker(results)

Cross-source merge (the default fan-in): fuse by rank, never by raw score.

Groups the accumulated pool by `hit.source` and delegates the merge to
`ir.fuse_hits()` (ir is the SSOT for hit operations): within each
source raw scores order and dedup that source’s hits — one scale, sound —
and across sources only **ranks** interact (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), so
heterogeneous embedders / modes can never mis-order the merge, and
colliding `artifact_id`s from different sources stay distinct results
(identity is `(source, artifact_id)`).

A single-source pool (or an untagged one — hits with no `source`) keeps
its raw scores and exactly [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.score_reranker)’s ordering; fused,
rank-derived scores only appear when there is genuinely something to fuse.
Each fused hit keeps its pre-fusion magnitude as
`metadata["source_score"]`. For per-source weights, another `rrf_k`,
or opt-in cross-source duplicate merging, use [`make_rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.make_rrf_reranker).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.agent.score_reranker(results)

Magnitude merge: one surface per artifact, ordered by descending raw score.

Delegates to `ir.base.best_per_artifact()` (ir is the SSOT for hit
operations): an artifact retrieved by several queries / rounds — common once
the back-edge re-queries — survives once, at its highest score. Identity is
`(source, artifact_id)`, so two sources’ same-id artifacts never collapse.

A plain score sort compares raw scores **across** sources, which is only
sound when every source shares one score scale (same embedder + mode) — it
is the explicit homogeneous-sources opt-in. The default fan-in is
[`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.rrf_reranker), which never compares raw scores across sources.

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.agent.single_subtask_planner(query, sources)

Trivial planner: one sub-task over *all* registered sources, no decomposition.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask)]


# _autosummary/raglab.html.md

# raglab

`raglab` — the agentic-search / RAG orchestration layer on top of `ir`.

`raglab` turns a retrieval substrate into a *Composable Search Agent* (the ir_09
architecture): a small set of injected **roles** — Planner, Formulator,
Retriever, Evaluator, Reranker, Citer — wired by a control loop whose back-edge
(evaluator → reformulate) is what makes it an agent rather than a DAG. Concrete
tools live at the leaves: an `ir` corpus becomes one `Retriever` via
`ir.as_retriever`.

Quick start (the no-LLM thin slice — runs offline):

```default
import ir
import raglab

# register ir corpora as the agent's sources, then search across them:
sources = raglab.ir_sources("skills", "reports", mode="hybrid")
agent = raglab.make_search_agent(sources)
results = agent("how do I deploy the app")      # ranked ir.SearchHits
```

Inject an LLM `formulator` (query rewrite/HyDE) and `evaluator` (sufficiency

+ refinement) to turn on query understanding and the back-edge. Dependency
  direction is one-way: `raglab` imports `ir`; `ir` never imports `raglab`.

> Fresh start (v0.2.0+). This repo took over the `raglab` PyPI name; the older
> backend now lives at `raglab_bak`. Development is just beginning.

### *class* raglab.GradedLabel(level, is_about, is_supported, is_useful, evidence_quote='', facet=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A graded verdict on one candidate (raglab#8): a level, three axes, the evidence.

`level` is one of the evaluator’s ordered levels (best first). The axes are
Self-RAG’s: `is_about` (topical, ISREL), `is_supported` (the content
actually establishes it, not a lexical mention: ISSUP) and `is_useful`
(ISUSE). `evidence_quote` is a verbatim span of the candidate’s content
backing the level; `facet` names the sub-goal it was judged against.

### *class* raglab.Judgement(relevant, sufficient, refinement=None, graded=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

An evaluator’s verdict over a round’s results.

`relevant` is the kept subset; `sufficient` says whether to stop; a
non-`None` `refinement` is the **back-edge** — the next sub-task to
re-query with. The pass-through default returns `sufficient=True` and no
refinement (no loop). `graded` is optional and additive: a graded
evaluator maps each judged `artifact_id` to its [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.GradedLabel);
binary evaluators leave it empty.

### *class* raglab.LowLevelQuery(source, query, params=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One concrete query against one source.

`query` is the text handed to the source’s `Retriever`; `params`
are per-call retriever overrides (e.g. `mode` / `filter` / `k` for an
ir corpus). A formulator turns a [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.SubTask) into these.

Bases: [`Protocol`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Protocol)

Bound the pool the evaluator sees to at most `limit` results.

A governor decision (which hits survive the budget), injected like every other
role so a strategy can be swapped without touching the loop. It must return
hits **unchanged** — never re-scored — because the pool keeps raw per-source
magnitudes until the fan-in reranker.

### raglab.Result

alias of `SearchHit`

### *class* raglab.RoundRecord(purpose, round, goal, sources, sufficient, refinement, committed, graded=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What one round of the loop decided: the run-log’s unit (raglab#6).

Written at the evaluator’s judgement point, it is the single record shape that
per-run observability (the run-log) and cross-run memory (a purpose store)
both consume. `purpose` is the sub-task’s original goal; `goal` is what this
round actually searched (a refinement, from round 1 on). `committed` holds the
hits the evaluator kept, with their **raw** per-source magnitudes: the pool never
carries fused scores, so neither does the record.

JSON-clean form: hits via `SearchHit.to_dict`, labels as plain dicts.

score – sound, since one source is one score scale – and deals hits round-robin
across the groups. So a late source’s strong hits are never cut before the evaluator
sees them, a duplicate never takes a slot, and no score ever crosses a source
boundary or is rewritten (unlike pre-ranking with the RRF reranker, whose fused
ordinal scores must never re-enter the pool). The output is in that dealt order
whatever the pool’s size. A missing or NaN score sorts last in its source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

#### reranker()

Cross-source merge (the default fan-in): fuse by rank, never by raw score.

Groups the accumulated pool by `hit.source` and delegates the merge to
`ir.fuse_hits()` (ir is the SSOT for hit operations): within each
source raw scores order and dedup that source’s hits — one scale, sound —
and across sources only **ranks** interact (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), so
heterogeneous embedders / modes can never mis-order the merge, and
colliding `artifact_id`s from different sources stay distinct results
(identity is `(source, artifact_id)`).

A single-source pool (or an untagged one — hits with no `source`) keeps
its raw scores and exactly [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.score_reranker)’s ordering; fused,
rank-derived scores only appear when there is genuinely something to fuse.
Each fused hit keeps its pre-fusion magnitude as
`metadata["source_score"]`. For per-source weights, another `rrf_k`,
or opt-in cross-source duplicate merging, use [`make_rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.make_rrf_reranker).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### *class* raglab.SubTask(goal, sources)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A planner’s unit of work: a sub-goal bound to a set of registered sources.

### raglab.apply_gates(proposed, content, , levels=('core', 'strong', 'uses-tools', 'tangential', 'none'), unsupported_cap='tangential', require_evidence_quote=True, calibration_offset=None, min_quote_chars=8)

The level a judge’s proposal is allowed, after calibration and the gates.

The quote must be at least `min_quote_chars` long and found in `content`,
ignoring case and runs of whitespace (judges re-case and re-wrap what they
copy). `calibration_offset` is in levels, rounded half up, so a shift is
the same at every level.

```pycon
>>> label = GradedLabel('core', True, False, True, 'a DAG of tasks')
>>> apply_gates(label, 'Runs a DAG of tasks asynchronously.').level
'tangential'
>>> ok = GradedLabel('core', True, True, True, 'graph  library')
>>> apply_gates(ok, 'A graph library.').level, apply_gates(ok, 'Nothing here.').level
('core', 'tangential')
>>> apply_gates(ok, 'A graph library.', calibration_offset=1.4).level
'strong'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel)

### raglab.arrival_order_cap(results, limit)

Keep the first `limit` hits in arrival order (source order x query order).

The pre-governor behaviour: a late source’s strong hits can be cut before the
evaluator sees them. Kept as an explicit opt-in (`pool_cap=arrival_order_cap`).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.identity_citer(results)

No-op citer (verification needs a generated claim — that lives in srag).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.identity_formulator(task, source)

Identity formulator: the sub-goal verbatim as one query (no rewrite/HyDE).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery)]

### raglab.ir_sources(\*names, \*\*search_defaults)

A source registry `{name: Retriever}` backed by named `ir` corpora.

Each name is bound to `ir.as_retriever(name, **search_defaults)`, opened
eagerly. For the *lazy* live view over everything registered (a corpus
opens only when its key is first used), use `ir.retrievers()` instead —
the agent accepts either, or any `Mapping[name, Retriever]`.
`search_defaults` (e.g. `mode="hybrid"`) apply to every source.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]]]

### raglab.make_graded_rubric_evaluator(, levels=('core', 'strong', 'uses-tools', 'tangential', 'none'), rubric="- core: the candidate's main purpose IS the topic.\\n- strong: a substantial, central part of the candidate is about the topic.\\n- uses-tools: the candidate builds on tools or libraries of the topic (its dependencies or imports establish it) without being about it.\\n- tangential: the topic is mentioned, or its vocabulary appears, but the content does not establish it.\\n- none: unrelated.\\n", judge=None, disclose_level='body', disclose_kwargs=None, require_evidence_quote=True, unsupported_cap='tangential', calibration_offset=None, min_quote_chars=8, relevant_level='uses-tools', refine=None, rng=None, prompt='Goal: {goal}\\n\\nRubric (levels, in no particular order):\\n{levels}\\n\\nDefinitions:\\n{rubric}\\n\\nCandidate {artifact_id}:\\n---\\n{content}\\n---\\n\\nAnswer with one JSON object and nothing else, with keys:\\n"is_about" (bool: is the candidate topically about the goal?),\\n"is_supported" (bool: does its content - code, dependencies, imports, full text - actually establish it, beyond a mention of the words?),\\n"is_useful" (bool: would it help someone pursuing the goal?),\\n"evidence_quote" (a short span copied VERBATIM from the candidate\\'s content that supports your level),\\n"level" (one of the rubric\\'s levels).\\n', max_content_chars=4000, \*\*prompt_function_kwargs)

An [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator) that grades every candidate on a rubric.

* **Parameters:**
  * **levels** ([`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the ordered levels, best first.
  * **rubric** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – what each level means, shown to the judge.
  * **judge** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – an injectable graded judge (a test double, or your own router);
    built lazily on `oa` when omitted.
  * **disclose_level** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – what the judge reads — each candidate’s
    content through `ir.disclose()` at that level (`store=` /
    `loader=` go in `disclose_kwargs`); a candidate with nothing to
    load is judged on its snippet.
  * **disclose_kwargs** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – what the judge reads — each candidate’s
    content through `ir.disclose()` at that level (`store=` /
    `loader=` go in `disclose_kwargs`); a candidate with nothing to
    load is judged on its snippet.
  * **require_evidence_quote** ([`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)) – min_quote_chars: the gates, see [`apply_gates()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.apply_gates).
  * **unsupported_cap** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – min_quote_chars: the gates, see [`apply_gates()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.apply_gates).
  * **calibration_offset** ([`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – min_quote_chars: the gates, see [`apply_gates()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.apply_gates).
* **Return type:**
  [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator)

:param : min_quote_chars: the gates, see [`apply_gates()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.apply_gates).
:type relevant_level: [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)
:param relevant_level: the lowest level kept in `Judgement.relevant`.
:type refine: [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel)]], [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)
:param refine: the back-edge policy `(task, graded) -> SubTask | None`; by

> default none, so the loop stops after one round.
* **Parameters:**
  **rng** ([`Random`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/random.html#random.Random) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the source of the per-call level order (seed it for reproducible
  prompts).
* **Return type:**
  [*Evaluator*](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator)

Every candidate is judged once per goal: one judge call per (source,
artifact) the first time it appears in a pool for that goal, its label
remembered for later rounds, so a kept hit is not re-judged (nor lost to a
later failing call). `Judgement.graded` is keyed by `artifact_id`; an id
found in several sources carries its best label. A reply that does not parse
leaves the candidate ungraded (logged); when every judge call of a round
raises, the first error is re-raised rather than returning an empty,
“sufficient” round. This evaluator is for labelling a pool, not for cheap
filtering.

### raglab.make_llm_evaluator(, judge=None, select_strategy='conservative', select_kwargs=None, prerank=None, prompt='A search agent is pursuing this goal:\\n\\n{goal}\\n\\nA calibrated selector reviewed the retrieved candidates and committed to the\\nresults below (it abstained if this list is empty):\\n\\n{results}\\n\\nDecide whether these results are SUFFICIENT to satisfy the goal.\\n- If they are, reply with exactly: SUFFICIENT\\n- If they are not, reply with: INSUFFICIENT\\n  then, on the next line, a single improved search query that would retrieve what\\n  is still missing. Keep it a terse search phrase — no prose, no numbering.\\n', max_result_chars=500, \*\*prompt_function_kwargs)

An LLM-backed raglab [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator) (turns on the back-edge).

Relevance is ir’s: each round the accumulated results are passed through
`ir.select()` and the committed subset becomes the `Judgement.relevant`
(so the LLM stays in its lane — LLM relevance is known-fragile, ir_01 §3).
Sufficiency is the LLM’s: it reads the committed subset (informed by ir’s
model-free `sufficient` hint via abstention) and decides
whether the goal is satisfied. When it is not, the judge’s improved query
becomes a `refinement` [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask) over the same sources
— the **back-edge**.

* **Parameters:**
  * **judge** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – an injectable `(goal, results) -> (sufficient, refinement)`
    callable (a test double, or your own router); a raw text reply is also
    accepted and parsed. When omitted it is built lazily on `oa`.
  * **select_strategy** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ir selection strategy for the relevance decision
    (default `"conservative"` — distractor-robust).
  * **select_kwargs** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – extra args forwarded to `ir.select()`
    (e.g. `max_k`, `rel`). `min_score` is allowed only while the
    round’s pool keeps raw scores (single-source, or
    `prerank=score_reranker`): an absolute floor is per-(corpus,
    mode, embedder), so a round whose pool was rank-fused across
    sources **raises** rather than silently mass-abstaining on
    ordinal RRF scores.
  * **prerank** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Reranker) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the per-round merge that puts the accumulated pool best-first
    (and deduped) before `ir.select`. Defaults to
    [`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.rrf_reranker) — a round’s pool can already mix
    sources (a SubTask spans several), so the same rank-based,
    scale-safe merge as the fan-in applies; single-source rounds keep
    raw scores. Inject [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.score_reranker) for
    sources known to share one score scale.
  * **max_result_chars** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – per-result text truncation in the judge prompt.
* **Return type:**
  [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator)

Safe fallback: any judge error returns `refinement=None` — the control
loop’s break condition — so a failing judge can never fabricate an endless
loop. Sufficiency without a refinement query is likewise treated as a stop.

### raglab.make_llm_formulator(, formulate=None, params=None, \*\*make_kwargs)

An LLM-backed raglab [`Formulator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Formulator).

Adapts an ir-style query formulator (`str -> str | [str]`) to the role
contract `(SubTask, source) -> [LowLevelQuery]`: the sub-goal text is
rewritten / expanded into one or more search queries, each wrapped as a
[`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery) against `source`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **formulate** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – an injectable ir-style formulator (a test double, or one you
    built). When omitted it is built once via
    `ir.make_llm_formulator()` (`**make_kwargs` are forwarded —
    e.g. `n`, `prompt`, `rewriter`); that call is offline (`oa` is
    imported lazily only when the formulator is *invoked*), so
    `import raglab` stays offline.
  * **params** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – per-call retriever overrides (e.g. `{"mode": "hybrid", "k": 5}`)
    attached to every emitted [`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery).
* **Return type:**
  [`Formulator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Formulator)

The boundary: this returns **queries, never SubTasks**. ir’s formulator
already falls back to identity on any failure, so the emitted list is never
empty — a formulator must never make retrieval worse than the raw sub-goal.

### raglab.make_rrf_reranker(, rrf_k=60, weights=None, identity=None)

A parametrized [`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.rrf_reranker) (per-source trust weights, `rrf_k`).

* **Parameters:**
  * **rrf_k** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – the RRF rank constant (standard default 60).
  * **weights** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – optional per-source trust dial, by source name (default 1.0
    each) — biases the merge without ever comparing raw scores.
  * **identity** ([`Union`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Union)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`SearchHit`], [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)]) – opt-in cross-source duplicate detection (e.g. `"pointer"`)
    — see `ir.retrieve.Identity`. Default: never merge across
    sources.
* **Return type:**
  [`Reranker`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Reranker)

### raglab.make_search_agent(sources, , planner=None, formulator=None, evaluator=None, reranker=None, citer=None, budget=None, pool_cap=None, run_log=None)

Build a [`SingleContextAgent`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.SingleContextAgent) over *sources* with smart defaults.

`sources` is a `Mapping[name, Retriever]` — e.g.
`{"skills": ir.as_retriever("skills")}`, [`ir_sources()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.ir_sources), or the lazy
`ir.retrievers()` view. Every role defaults to its no-LLM thin-slice
implementation, so `make_search_agent(sources)("query")` just works;
inject an LLM `formulator` / `evaluator` to turn on rewriting and the
back-edge. Pass a `run_log` (any callable taking a [`RoundRecord`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.RoundRecord), e.g.
`list.append`) to record what each round decided.

A custom `Retriever` must return `ir.SearchHit` instances (the
`Result` alias): the loop stamps provenance (`hit.source`) on its
output, so duck-typed hit objects raise at the tagging step.

* **Return type:**
  [`SingleContextAgent`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SingleContextAgent)

### raglab.passthrough_evaluator(task, results)

Pass-through critic: keep everything, declare sufficient, never re-query.

* **Return type:**
  [`Judgement`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Judgement)

### raglab.rank_fair_cap(results, limit)

Keep at most `limit` hits, taking the best of each source in turn (the default).

Groups the pool by `hit.source` (in first-arrival order; untagged hits are one
group), collapses each group to one hit per artifact (its best surface, as
`ir.base.best_per_artifact()` does), orders the group best-first by its own raw
score – sound, since one source is one score scale – and deals hits round-robin
across the groups. So a late source’s strong hits are never cut before the evaluator
sees them, a duplicate never takes a slot, and no score ever crosses a source
boundary or is rewritten (unlike pre-ranking with the RRF reranker, whose fused
ordinal scores must never re-enter the pool). The output is in that dealt order
whatever the pool’s size. A missing or NaN score sorts last in its source.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.rrf_reranker(results)

Cross-source merge (the default fan-in): fuse by rank, never by raw score.

Groups the accumulated pool by `hit.source` and delegates the merge to
`ir.fuse_hits()` (ir is the SSOT for hit operations): within each
source raw scores order and dedup that source’s hits — one scale, sound —
and across sources only **ranks** interact (Reciprocal Rank Fusion), so
heterogeneous embedders / modes can never mis-order the merge, and
colliding `artifact_id`s from different sources stay distinct results
(identity is `(source, artifact_id)`).

A single-source pool (or an untagged one — hits with no `source`) keeps
its raw scores and exactly [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.score_reranker)’s ordering; fused,
rank-derived scores only appear when there is genuinely something to fuse.
Each fused hit keeps its pre-fusion magnitude as
`metadata["source_score"]`. For per-source weights, another `rrf_k`,
or opt-in cross-source duplicate merging, use [`make_rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.make_rrf_reranker).

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.score_reranker(results)

Magnitude merge: one surface per artifact, ordered by descending raw score.

Delegates to `ir.base.best_per_artifact()` (ir is the SSOT for hit
operations): an artifact retrieved by several queries / rounds — common once
the back-edge re-queries — survives once, at its highest score. Identity is
`(source, artifact_id)`, so two sources’ same-id artifacts never collapse.

A plain score sort compares raw scores **across** sources, which is only
sound when every source shares one score scale (same embedder + mode) — it
is the explicit homogeneous-sources opt-in. The default fan-in is
[`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.rrf_reranker), which never compares raw scores across sources.

* **Return type:**
  [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[`SearchHit`]

### raglab.single_subtask_planner(query, sources)

Trivial planner: one sub-task over *all* registered sources, no decomposition.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask)]

# _autosummary/raglab.judging.html.md

# raglab.judging

Graded rubric judging — every candidate gets a level, three axes and evidence (raglab#8).

A binary relevant/not cannot say “mentions the word but is not about it”. The
evaluator built by [`make_graded_rubric_evaluator()`](_autosummary/raglab.judging.html.md#raglab.judging.make_graded_rubric_evaluator) asks an injected judge,
for **each** candidate in the round’s pool, for the three Self-RAG axes
(`is_about`, `is_supported`, `is_useful`), a level on an ordered scale and
a verbatim `evidence_quote` from the candidate’s disclosed content. The judge
proposes; deterministic gates here dispose:

- a level above `unsupported_cap` needs `is_supported` — topical vocabulary
  without supporting content is capped (the direct fix for on-word distractors);
- with `require_evidence_quote`, it also needs a quote found verbatim in the
  content the judge was shown (whitespace-insensitive);
- `calibration_offset` (levels, learned from a gold slice) shifts every level
  down (positive: the judge over-grades) or up;
- the level options are shown in a fresh random order on every call, against
  position bias.

The result is a [`Judgement`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Judgement) whose additive `graded` map
carries every label, whose `relevant` keeps the candidates at or above
`relevant_level`, and whose back-edge comes from an injected `refine` policy
(none by default: the loop stops). As in [`raglab.llm`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#module-raglab.llm), the default judge is
built lazily on `oa`, so `import raglab` stays offline, and a judge that
fails on a candidate leaves it ungraded rather than guessing.

### raglab.judging.DEFAULT_TOPICAL_RUBRIC *= "- core: the candidate's main purpose IS the topic.\\n- strong: a substantial, central part of the candidate is about the topic.\\n- uses-tools: the candidate builds on tools or libraries of the topic (its dependencies or imports establish it) without being about it.\\n- tangential: the topic is mentioned, or its vocabulary appears, but the content does not establish it.\\n- none: unrelated.\\n"*

What the default levels mean, for a “is this package about TOPIC” question.

### raglab.judging.GRADING_PROMPT *= 'Goal: {goal}\\n\\nRubric (levels, in no particular order):\\n{levels}\\n\\nDefinitions:\\n{rubric}\\n\\nCandidate {artifact_id}:\\n---\\n{content}\\n---\\n\\nAnswer with one JSON object and nothing else, with keys:\\n"is_about" (bool: is the candidate topically about the goal?),\\n"is_supported" (bool: does its content - code, dependencies, imports, full text - actually establish it, beyond a mention of the words?),\\n"is_useful" (bool: would it help someone pursuing the goal?),\\n"evidence_quote" (a short span copied VERBATIM from the candidate\\'s content that supports your level),\\n"level" (one of the rubric\\'s levels).\\n'*

### raglab.judging.apply_gates(proposed, content, , levels=('core', 'strong', 'uses-tools', 'tangential', 'none'), unsupported_cap='tangential', require_evidence_quote=True, calibration_offset=None, min_quote_chars=8)

The level a judge’s proposal is allowed, after calibration and the gates.

The quote must be at least `min_quote_chars` long and found in `content`,
ignoring case and runs of whitespace (judges re-case and re-wrap what they
copy). `calibration_offset` is in levels, rounded half up, so a shift is
the same at every level.

```pycon
>>> label = GradedLabel('core', True, False, True, 'a DAG of tasks')
>>> apply_gates(label, 'Runs a DAG of tasks asynchronously.').level
'tangential'
>>> ok = GradedLabel('core', True, True, True, 'graph  library')
>>> apply_gates(ok, 'A graph library.').level, apply_gates(ok, 'Nothing here.').level
('core', 'tangential')
>>> apply_gates(ok, 'A graph library.', calibration_offset=1.4).level
'strong'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel)

> default none, so the loop stops after one round.
* **Parameters:**
  **rng** ([`Random`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/random.html#random.Random) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the source of the per-call level order (seed it for reproducible
  prompts).
* **Return type:**
  [*Evaluator*](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator)

Every candidate is judged once per goal: one judge call per (source,
artifact) the first time it appears in a pool for that goal, its label
remembered for later rounds, so a kept hit is not re-judged (nor lost to a
later failing call). `Judgement.graded` is keyed by `artifact_id`; an id
found in several sources carries its best label. A reply that does not parse
leaves the candidate ungraded (logged); when every judge call of a round
raises, the first error is re-raised rather than returning an empty,
“sufficient” round. This evaluator is for labelling a pool, not for cheap
filtering.


# _autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md

# raglab.llm

LLM-backed roles — the Formulator and Evaluator (ir_09 §8 steps 1 & 3).

`raglab`’s no-LLM thin slice ([`raglab.agent`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#module-raglab.agent)) runs offline: an identity
formulator and a pass-through evaluator. This module supplies the two LLM roles
that turn that slice into a real agent — query understanding and the back-edge:

- [`make_llm_formulator()`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.make_llm_formulator) — query rewrite / expand / HyDE. A thin adapter
  over ir’s `ir.make_llm_formulator()` (the `formulate=` seam, ir_09 §3):
  ir owns the lazy-`oa` rewriter and the identity fallback; raglab only
  adapts the shape `str -> str | [str]` to the role contract
  `(SubTask, source) -> [LowLevelQuery]`.
- [`make_llm_evaluator()`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.make_llm_evaluator) — sufficiency + refinement. `ir.select` owns the
  *relevance* decision (the calibrated committed subset, ir_09 §3); the LLM owns
  *sufficiency* — informed by ir’s model-free `ir.Selection.sufficient`
  hint, it judges whether the committed subset actually satisfies the goal and,
  when it does not, emits a `refinement` SubTask. That refinement is the
  **back-edge** that makes the loop an agent rather than a DAG.

Two load-bearing boundaries (ir ↔ raglab), guarded here:

1. A Formulator returns **queries, never SubTasks** — decomposition is the
   Planner’s job. [`make_llm_formulator()`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.make_llm_formulator) only ever yields
   [`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery)s.
2. The **back-edge lives in raglab**, never in ir: ir derives a `sufficient`
   *signal* from its own selection; raglab’s Evaluator is what reads it, decides,
   and re-queries.

Both builders mirror `ir.select.make_llm_selector()`: an injectable callable
(a test double, or your own router), built lazily on `oa` only when omitted
(so `import raglab` stays offline), with a **safe fallback** — a formulator must
never make retrieval worse than the raw query, and an evaluator must never
fabricate an endless loop (on any failure it returns no refinement, which is the
loop’s break condition).

### Module Attributes

| [`EVALUATION_PROMPT`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.EVALUATION_PROMPT)   | Default prompt for [`make_llm_evaluator()`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.make_llm_evaluator) — judge sufficiency, else emit a single improved query (the refinement that drives the back-edge).   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`make_llm_evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.llm.html.md#raglab.llm.make_llm_evaluator)(\*[, judge, ...])           | An LLM-backed raglab [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator) (turns on the back-edge). |

### raglab.llm.EVALUATION_PROMPT *= 'A search agent is pursuing this goal:\\n\\n{goal}\\n\\nA calibrated selector reviewed the retrieved candidates and committed to the\\nresults below (it abstained if this list is empty):\\n\\n{results}\\n\\nDecide whether these results are SUFFICIENT to satisfy the goal.\\n- If they are, reply with exactly: SUFFICIENT\\n- If they are not, reply with: INSUFFICIENT\\n  then, on the next line, a single improved search query that would retrieve what\\n  is still missing. Keep it a terse search phrase — no prose, no numbering.\\n'*

single improved query (the refinement that drives the back-edge).

### raglab.llm.make_llm_evaluator(, judge=None, select_strategy='conservative', select_kwargs=None, prerank=None, prompt='A search agent is pursuing this goal:\\n\\n{goal}\\n\\nA calibrated selector reviewed the retrieved candidates and committed to the\\nresults below (it abstained if this list is empty):\\n\\n{results}\\n\\nDecide whether these results are SUFFICIENT to satisfy the goal.\\n- If they are, reply with exactly: SUFFICIENT\\n- If they are not, reply with: INSUFFICIENT\\n  then, on the next line, a single improved search query that would retrieve what\\n  is still missing. Keep it a terse search phrase — no prose, no numbering.\\n', max_result_chars=500, \*\*prompt_function_kwargs)

An LLM-backed raglab [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator) (turns on the back-edge).

Relevance is ir’s: each round the accumulated results are passed through
`ir.select()` and the committed subset becomes the `Judgement.relevant`
(so the LLM stays in its lane — LLM relevance is known-fragile, ir_01 §3).
Sufficiency is the LLM’s: it reads the committed subset (informed by ir’s
model-free `sufficient` hint via abstention) and decides
whether the goal is satisfied. When it is not, the judge’s improved query
becomes a `refinement` [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask) over the same sources
— the **back-edge**.

* **Parameters:**
  * **judge** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`bool`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)] | [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]) – an injectable `(goal, results) -> (sufficient, refinement)`
    callable (a test double, or your own router); a raw text reply is also
    accepted and parsed. When omitted it is built lazily on `oa`.
  * **select_strategy** ([`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)) – ir selection strategy for the relevance decision
    (default `"conservative"` — distractor-robust).
  * **select_kwargs** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – extra args forwarded to `ir.select()`
    (e.g. `max_k`, `rel`). `min_score` is allowed only while the
    round’s pool keeps raw scores (single-source, or
    `prerank=score_reranker`): an absolute floor is per-(corpus,
    mode, embedder), so a round whose pool was rank-fused across
    sources **raises** rather than silently mass-abstaining on
    ordinal RRF scores.
  * **prerank** ([`Reranker`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Reranker) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the per-round merge that puts the accumulated pool best-first
    (and deduped) before `ir.select`. Defaults to
    [`rrf_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.rrf_reranker) — a round’s pool can already mix
    sources (a SubTask spans several), so the same rank-based,
    scale-safe merge as the fan-in applies; single-source rounds keep
    raw scores. Inject [`score_reranker()`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.score_reranker) for
    sources known to share one score scale.
  * **max_result_chars** ([`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)) – per-result text truncation in the judge prompt.
* **Return type:**
  [`Evaluator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Evaluator)

Safe fallback: any judge error returns `refinement=None` — the control
loop’s break condition — so a failing judge can never fabricate an endless
loop. Sufficiency without a refinement query is likewise treated as a stop.

### raglab.llm.make_llm_formulator(, formulate=None, params=None, \*\*make_kwargs)

An LLM-backed raglab [`Formulator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Formulator).

Adapts an ir-style query formulator (`str -> str | [str]`) to the role
contract `(SubTask, source) -> [LowLevelQuery]`: the sub-goal text is
rewritten / expanded into one or more search queries, each wrapped as a
[`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery) against `source`.

* **Parameters:**
  * **formulate** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)], [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str) | [`Sequence`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Sequence)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]]]) – an injectable ir-style formulator (a test double, or one you
    built). When omitted it is built once via
    `ir.make_llm_formulator()` (`**make_kwargs` are forwarded —
    e.g. `n`, `prompt`, `rewriter`); that call is offline (`oa` is
    imported lazily only when the formulator is *invoked*), so
    `import raglab` stays offline.
  * **params** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – per-call retriever overrides (e.g. `{"mode": "hybrid", "k": 5}`)
    attached to every emitted [`LowLevelQuery`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.LowLevelQuery).
* **Return type:**
  [`Formulator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Formulator)

The boundary: this returns **queries, never SubTasks**. ir’s formulator
already falls back to identity on any failure, so the emitted list is never
empty — a formulator must never make retrieval worse than the raw sub-goal.


# _autosummary/raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.html.md

# raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling

Label a corpus against a topic, facet by facet, with a graded judge (raglab#8, part B).

[`label_corpus()`](_autosummary/raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.html.md#raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.label_corpus) composes existing pieces and adds no orchestrator:

- a planner that emits one [`SubTask`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SubTask) per **facet** of the
  topic, for broad recall;
- a formulator (identity by default; [`raglab.make_llm_formulator()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.make_llm_formulator) for
  query expansion);
- the graded rubric evaluator ([`raglab.make_graded_rubric_evaluator()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.make_graded_rubric_evaluator)),
  which judges **every** retrieved candidate on its disclosed content;
- a **coverage** check per facet (enough candidates at `coverage_level`),
  which, when a facet looks thin and a `reformulate` policy is given, emits a
  refinement sub-task: the back-edge of [`SingleContextAgent`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.SingleContextAgent).

The deliverable is a frozen [`CorpusLabeling`](_autosummary/raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.html.md#raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.CorpusLabeling): each judged artifact’s best
[`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel) (its `facet` set) and each facet’s coverage.
Nothing here touches `ir`; the corpus is read through a retriever
(`ir.as_retriever()` by default).

| [`label_corpus`](_autosummary/raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.html.md#raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.label_corpus)(corpus, \*, facets[, retriever, ...])   | Label `corpus` for each of `facets` with a graded judge; see the module.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|

  * **facets** ([`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)] | [`Iterable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Iterable)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]) – the topic’s facets, as `{name: goal}` or names (a name is its
    own goal). One sub-task each.
  * **retriever** ([`Optional`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Optional)[[`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), list[SearchHit]]]) – inject a `Retriever` instead (a test
    double, a federated source); `corpus` is then not read.
  * **formulator** ([`Formulator`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Formulator)) – the Formulator role (identity, or
    [`raglab.make_llm_formulator()`](_autosummary/raglab.html.md#raglab.make_llm_formulator)).
  * **judge** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[`...`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#Ellipsis), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the graded judge (built lazily on `oa` when omitted).
  * **reformulate** ([`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Callable)[[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`GradedLabel`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.GradedLabel)]], str | None] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – gap-driven reformulation; when a facet has fewer than
    `min_covered` labels at `coverage_level` it gets a new query, which
    becomes the facet’s next sub-task. `None` (default): one round each.
  * **budget** ([`Budget`](_autosummary/raglab.agent.html.md#raglab.agent.Budget) | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)) – the loop bounds (`max_rounds` caps the reformulations).
  * **\*\*evaluator_kwargs** ([`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)) – forwarded to
    [`make_graded_rubric_evaluator()`](_autosummary/raglab.judging.html.md#raglab.judging.make_graded_rubric_evaluator) (`rubric`,
    `calibration_offset`, `disclose_kwargs`, `rng`, …).
* **Return type:**
  [`CorpusLabeling`](_autosummary/raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.html.md#raglab.recipes.corpus_labeling.CorpusLabeling)

# For AI agents

`raglab` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/raglab/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/raglab/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`raglab.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/raglab/raglab.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/raglab/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
